  "summary": "This English-language Swarajya extract, published for Rajaji’s birthday, presents C. Rajagopalachari through a series of recollections and tributes drawn from Masti Venkatesa Iyengar’s book Rajaji. The opening characterizes Rajaji as an intellectually gifted, self-sacrificing statesman whose public achievements were matched by an inner moral and personal greatness. Recollections by G. Ramachandran and C. F. Andrews emphasize his calmness, modesty, intimacy with Gandhi, and ability to inspire confidence in moments of national uncertainty.\n\nThe second part focuses on Rajaji’s public administration and personal qualities. It recalls his premiership of Madras, including his removal of a controversial statue of Neil, and depicts him as resourceful, intellectually keen, articulate, courageous, and guided by integrity. Tributes from Rajendra Prasad, Vallabhbhai Patel, and Jawaharlal Nehru portray him as a lifelong colleague of Gandhi and Nehru, a wise crisis-manager, and an exceptionally self-sacrificing national asset. The accompanying cartoon page comments satirically on leadership, foreign influence, coercive rule, and the distribution of political seats; the final page is a portrait sketch of Rajaji.",
